subject: Publisher embargo windows & weights access — distribution terms review
messages:
From: Diego Ramos <diego.r@openatlas.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: partners@openatlas.ai
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Publisher distribution — initial terms and embargo question

Hi Camila —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. We ran the community board conversation and there's interest in a pilot distribution agreement with Redwood for our Atlas-Large-12 model weights. Before we get into pricing, there are two publisher-side constraints I want to be transparent about:

1) Short embargo window: we require a 30–60 day embargo from first public distribution by partners where redistribution of raw weights to third parties is blocked.
2) Access tiers: we want to permit hosted inference + co-hosting on approved partners, but we prefer to restrict mirrored public downloads without an explicit redistribution license.

I've attached a very rough draft (Atlas_Publisher_Terms_Draft_vA.docx) so you can see the shape of the clauses. Two asks from our side to move quickly:
- Can Redwood commit to an audit trail for who had weight-level access and for how long (we know you have token-level tracing; we'd like something we can rely on for compliance)?
- Is an embargo enforcement mechanism feasible on your Dedicated/Private offerings (e.g., a flag that disables model mirror endpoints for a contract period)?

Happy to sync — Diego (partners) and I can take a short call if that's easier.

Best,
Diego Ramos
Head of Ecosystem Partnerships
AtlasModel Collective
attachments: Atlas_Publisher_Terms_Draft_vA.docx

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Diego Ramos <diego.r@openatlas.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Publisher distribution — initial terms and embargo question

Diego —

Thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the draft. High level response from Redwood: we can support both an operational embargo flag and detailed access logs, but we need to clarify scope and tooling. A few initial points:

- Audit trail: Redwood can provide time-bound access logs (who requested model-level weights, when, and from which IP/region) as part of our Private and Dedicated tiers. We can add an exportable CSV and an API endpoint for automated attestations.
- Embargo enforcement: we can implement an "embargo mode" on model artifacts; when enabled it prevents creation of mirror/download endpoints and blocks export of raw weights from running instances. That capability exists but requires explicit contract-level enforcement and verification steps in our deployment automation.
- Commercials: short embargo windows are workable; we typically map embargo tightness to pricing/indemnity and can propose a staged distribution model (pilot: 30 days, then 60 days for wider distribution) with milestone-based escrow release.

Couple of asks on our side before drafting a formal MOU:
1) Which license you expect downstream partners to have (non-commercial research only vs. commercial redistributions)?
2) Any mandated security/compliance artifacts beyond SOC 2 (e.g., stricter KMS/HSM requirements, on-prem air-gapped hosting approvals)?

I've looped in Marissa (legal) and Jonas (partnerships) to weigh in. If you're available next week, propose Tuesday 10–11 PT for a 30-min working session.

—Camila
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-29T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Publisher distribution — initial terms and embargo question

Camila / Jonas —

Quick read of Atlas' draft: high-level notes (legal):

- Embargo clause: 30–60 days OK but define start trigger precisely — we recommend "first public distribution date as evidenced by a signed timestamped manifest" or an agreed delivery notice. Avoid vague language like "first public use."
- Redistribution prohibition: Acceptable, but we need carve-outs for (a) internal debugging by Redwood ops with strong logging, (b) emergency export for legal/regulatory requests.
- Audit/attestation: Redwood can commit to providing logs, but any contractual attestation should be time-boxed and limited to metadata (who/when) rather than copies of payloads. Atlas asking for copies of raw weights is a red flag.
- Enforcement: recommend a technical appendix that maps embargo flags to runtime actions (disable mirror endpoint, block snapshot export, audit hooks). We'll draft a short SLA matrix (see SLA_matrix.csv) that ties response times and verification windows to embargo enforcement.

I'll prepare a markup and a short MOU skeleton that preserves Atlas' embargo intent while protecting Redwood's operational flexibility. Draft will be uploaded to the shared drive and I'll attach a PDF here when ready.

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
attachments: SLA_matrix.csv

From: Diego Ramos <diego.r@openatlas.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: partners@openatlas.ai
Date: 2026-05-31T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Publisher distribution — initial terms and embargo question

Camila/Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed clarifications — helpful. A couple of follow-ups from Atlas:

- Trigger: we can accept a signed manifest as trigger; will your team be able to verify and keep that manifest on record?
- Downstream license: default should be "no redistribution of raw weights" unless a downstream partner signs a redistribution addendum approved by Atlas. We want hosted inference allowed, plus classifiers/embeddings derived products, but not raw weights moving to other clouds.
- Attestation: Atlas doesn't need raw weight copies; the metadata logs you described are fine. We do want a dedicated audit path for the pilot cohort (3 partners max) so Atlas can verify no mirrors were created.

Happy to take the 30-min call on Tuesday 10 PT to walk a couple of specific use cases and the pilot partner list.

Diego
Head of Ecosystem Partnerships, AtlasModel Collective

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Diego Ramos <diego.r@openatlas.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-02T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Publisher distribution — initial terms and embargo question

Diego —

Appreciate the alignment. Quick summary and next steps we will take on Redwood's side before the Tuesday call:

1) Tech implementation note: we'll enable an "embargo mode" flag (template change) that prevents creating mirror/download endpoints and blocks model artifact export from UI/CLI for the contract period. Ops will log export attempts with an automated webhook to Atlas for pilot partners.
2) Legal: Marissa will upload a Redwood-marked MOU (Redwood_MOU_markup_20260529.pdf) to the drive with the proposed trigger language (signed manifest) and carve-outs for emergency/regulatory export.
3) Pilot: we'll scope a 30-day pilot for up to 3 partners; during pilot Atlas will get weekly CSV exports of access logs filtered to the pilot cohort. SLA matrix attached to our draft (SLA_matrix.csv).

Proposed meeting: Tuesday 2026-06-08 10:00 PT, 30 minutes — invite to follow from Jonas. If that works, please confirm and share the pilot partner names (3 max) so we can pre-configure audit hooks.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

—Camila
Head of Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_MOU_markup_20260529.pdf, SLA_matrix.csv
